network.overall_strategy: Most literature-supported routes to glutamate converge on the C5 alpha-keto hub 2-oxoglutarate, reached from pyruvate plus glyoxylate, 3-oxalomalate, 2-hydroxyglutarate, or a hydrothermal C6 amino-hydroxy precursor; nitrogen is then installed by either Fe0/Fe2+-hydroxylamine or FeS-ammonia reductive amination. A separate cyanosulfidic aminodinitrile branch supplies an independent surface-only route. The 10 pathways listed are the literature-guided distinct routes emphasized here, and the target node is non-stereospecific glutamate because the cited prebiotic syntheses are racemic.

reactions.name: Fe2+-catalyzed aldol condensation of pyruvate and glyoxylate

conditions.other: anoxic vent-mixing-zone water; Fe2+-rich; near-neutral to mildly alkaline

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+ activation of pyruvate enables aldol addition to the aldehyde carbonyl of glyoxylate, forming the new C-C bond of the C5 product.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) directly demonstrated Fe2+-promoted conversion of pyruvate and glyoxylate to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate at about 343 K, and Springsteen et al. (2018) observed the same C3+C2 condensation within linked glyoxylate cycles. This is the best-supported carbon-skeleton-building entry into the glutamate network under iron-rich anoxic hydrothermal conditions.

reactions.name: Dehydration of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic vent-mixing-zone water; dehydration of the beta-hydroxy ketoacid

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+-assisted beta-elimination removes water from the beta-hydroxy ketoacid to give the conjugated unsaturated keto-diacid.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) identified dehydration of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate to the conjugated enedione within the same iron-driven network. The step is chemically reasonable in warm aqueous Fe2+ solutions, although back-hydration and competing side reactions could lower natural yields.

reactions.name: Reduction of 4-oxopent-2-enedioic acid to 2-oxoglutarate
reactions.mechanism: Reduction of the C=C bond in the unsaturated keto-diacid yields the saturated alpha-keto acid 2-oxoglutarate.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) reported reduction of the unsaturated C5 intermediate to 2-oxoglutarate under the same Fe2+-rich conditions. Lee et al. (2014) showed that 2-oxoglutarate is a recurrent hydrothermal product, but also noted broader keto-acid interconversion and decomposition chemistry, so retention of 2-oxoglutarate depends on kinetic context.

reactions.name: Fe0/Fe2+-promoted reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with hydroxylamine

conditions.other: hydroxylamine present; Fe0 supplies electrons; racemic product expected

reactions.mechanism: Oxime or imine formation at the alpha-keto group is followed by iron-mediated reduction to furnish the alpha-amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) experimentally converted 2-oxoglutarate to glutamate by iron-promoted reductive amination with hydroxylamine. This is a strong mechanistic precedent, but the route is not uncritically preferred because prebiotic hydroxylamine abundance is debated; the product would also be racemic, so the network uses non-stereospecific glutamate.

reactions.name: FeS-catalyzed reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with ammonia

conditions.other: alkaline vent, pH 9-11, H2-rich and anoxic; racemic product expected

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia forms an imine with the alpha-keto group on FeS surfaces, and mineral-mediated reduction yields the amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Kitadai et al. (2019) showed FeS catalyzes reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate with ammonia in alkaline hydrothermal settings. This route is geochemically attractive because FeS is common at vents and NH3 is a more plausible nitrogen donor than hydroxylamine, though direct selectivity comparisons against the Fe0/Fe2+ system remain open; the product is expected to be racemic.

reactions.name: Amination of 2-hydroxypentane-1,5-dinitrile

conditions.other: cyanosulfidic evaporitic pool; precursor pool from HCN-rich photochemistry; concentration during drying

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia replaces the alpha-hydroxyl functionality of the hydroxydinitrile, forming the aminodinitrile and water.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported amination of the C5 hydroxydinitrile to the corresponding aminodinitrile in cyanosulfidic chemistry. The transformation is experimentally grounded, but persistence of the C5 dinitrile pool under natural UV, pH cycling, and dilution has not been fully quantified.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of 2-aminopentane-1,5-dinitrile to glutamate

conditions.other: wet phases after concentration cycles; racemic product expected

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration to amides and then carboxylates converts both nitriles to the dicarboxylic amino acid, releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) demonstrated hydrolysis of the aminodinitrile branch to glutamate, making this the key surface route that bypasses 2-oxoglutarate. Its plausibility is strong in concentrated wet phases, although field-scale yields would depend on keeping hydrolysis competitive with photolysis and dispersal; the product is expected to be racemic.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal fluid with redox gradients; no discrete catalyst specified

reactions.mechanism: Alpha-hydroxy oxidation or dehydrogenation converts the C2 alcohol to the corresponding alpha-keto group.
reactions.reasoning: Lee et al. (2014) identified 2-hydroxyglutarate as a hydrothermal precursor or interconversion partner of 2-oxoglutarate. This makes alpha-hydroxy to alpha-keto oxidation a credible vent-process entry to the hub molecule, though the same hot-fluid chemistry can also drive further degradation.

reactions.name: Cyanosulfidic oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: UV-exposed cyanosulfidic waters with sulfur redox chemistry

reactions.mechanism: Cyanosulfidic redox chemistry oxidizes the C2 alcohol to the corresponding alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Ritson (2021) incorporated 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation to 2-oxoglutarate into a cyanosulfidic prebiotic Krebs-cycle analogue. This gives a surface route to the glutamate hub, but productive transfer of that hub into later amination chemistry remains a systems-level open question rather than a one-pot demonstration.

reactions.name: Decarboxylation of 3-oxalomalic acid to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: ambient aqueous glyoxylate-cycle analogue; anoxic; conversion observed over hours

reactions.mechanism: Oxidative decarboxylation removes one carboxyl group from the C6 tricarboxylate, generating the C5 hydroxy-keto diacid.
reactions.reasoning: Springsteen et al. (2018) observed oxidative decarboxylation of 3-oxalomalic acid to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate at room temperature in aqueous solution. The reaction strongly supports a surface source of the downstream C5 intermediate, although coupling this ambient-temperature step into the hotter iron-driven sequence has not yet been shown continuously.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal decomposition of 2-amino-4-hydroxy-4-methylpentanedioic acid to 2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal decomposition; no discrete catalyst specified

reactions.mechanism: Retro-aldol-like cleavage and oxidative deamination collapse the C6 amino-hydroxy dicarboxylate to 2-oxoglutarate plus NH3.
reactions.reasoning: Lee et al. (2014) showed that 2-amino-4-hydroxy-4-methylpentanedioic acid decomposes in hydrothermal fluids to 2-oxoglutarate plus ammonia. This route is less direct than the pyruvate-glyoxylate branch but important because it shows chemically richer amino-acid-like precursors can collapse onto the same central keto-acid hub.

pathways.name: Pyruvate-glyoxylate iron route with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: Hydrothermal Fe2+ aldol chemistry builds 2-oxoglutarate from pyruvate and glyoxylate, followed by Fe0/Fe2+-driven reductive amination with hydroxylamine.

pathways.name: Pyruvate-glyoxylate iron route with FeS-ammonia finish
pathways.description: The same hydrothermal C3+C2 assembly route reaches 2-oxoglutarate, but glutamate is completed by FeS-catalyzed reductive amination with ammonia.

pathways.name: Oxalomalate surface handoff with hydroxylamine finish
pathways.description: Surface oxidative decarboxylation supplies 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, which then enters the hydrothermal iron dehydration-reduction sequence before hydroxylamine amination.

pathways.name: Oxalomalate surface handoff with FeS-ammonia finish
pathways.description: A surface glyoxylate-cycle analogue generates 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, and hydrothermal processing converts it to glutamate through the FeS-ammonia amination step.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation plus hydroxylamine amination
pathways.description: 2-Hydroxyglutarate is oxidized in hydrothermal fluids to 2-oxoglutarate and then converted to glutamate by the Fe0/Fe2+-hydroxylamine system.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation plus FeS-ammonia amination
pathways.description: A hydrothermal alpha-hydroxy to alpha-keto oxidation feeds directly into vent-mineral reductive amination with ammonia.

pathways.name: Surface 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation plus hydroxylamine amination
pathways.description: Cyanosulfidic surface oxidation produces 2-oxoglutarate, which is then taken into hydrothermal iron chemistry and aminated with hydroxylamine.

pathways.name: Surface 2-hydroxyglutarate oxidation plus FeS-ammonia amination
pathways.description: Surface-generated 2-oxoglutarate is completed to glutamate in an alkaline hydrothermal vent setting on FeS with ammonia.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal C6 precursor collapse with ammonia self-supply
pathways.description: A hydrothermal amino-hydroxy C6 precursor decomposes to 2-oxoglutarate and NH3, which then feed FeS-catalyzed reductive amination to glutamate.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic dinitrile hydrolysis route
pathways.description: An independent surface pathway converts a hydroxydinitrile to an aminodinitrile and hydrolyzes both nitriles to glutamate, bypassing 2-oxoglutarate.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This canonical hydrothermal Muchowska-style sequence is well aligned with the literature and the intermediates are correctly organized, but rxn_003 and rxn_004 are conservation violations in the deterministic check. rxn_003 likely needs an explicit reductant such as H2, while rxn_004 omits the reductive bookkeeping for the Fe0/Fe2+-mediated amination and likely needs explicit coproducts or sacrificial iron accounting. Hydroxylamine use is literature-supported, but its availability remains an acknowledged challenge.
suggestions: Add an explicit reductant to rxn_003 rather than treating the reduction as stoichiometry-free.
Rewrite rxn_004 with explicit reducing equivalents and balanced coproducts; if Fe0 is consumed, represent it as a reactant.
State the hydrothermal conditions more explicitly to match the cited experiments.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The pyruvate-plus-glyoxylate branch and the FeS-mediated finish are both literature-grounded, so the route is strategically coherent. However, rxn_003 and rxn_005 fail the balance check. rxn_003 likely needs H2 or another explicit reductant, and rxn_005 at minimum needs a reducing equivalent for the reductive amination rather than leaving the FeS-promoted reduction implicit.
suggestions: Add explicit reductant bookkeeping to rxn_003.
Balance rxn_005 with H2 or another clearly defined source of reducing power.
Specify the hydrothermal vent conditions and FeS mineral context explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The Springsteen-style surface decarboxylation to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate is credible, but the downstream hydrothermal sequence inherits the unbalanced rxn_003 and rxn_004. The surface-to-hydrothermal handoff of mol_003 is plausible, yet it is only implicit here, so the route is literature-inspired rather than fully specified as a continuous pathway.
suggestions: Add an explicit transfer or handoff step for mol_003 between the surface and hydrothermal environments.
Balance rxn_003 with an explicit reductant.
Rewrite rxn_004 with explicit redox bookkeeping and balanced coproducts.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This mixed surface-to-hydrothermal route is well motivated by the literature, with oxalomalate decarboxylation feeding the 2-oxoglutarate branch. The main problems are still rxn_003 and rxn_005: the reduction to 2-oxoglutarate lacks an explicit reductant, and the FeS-catalyzed amination leaves the reducing equivalent implicit. The environmental handoff is plausible but should be made explicit.
suggestions: Add a transport/handoff step for mol_003 from surface water to a hydrothermal setting.
Balance rxn_003 with an explicit reductant such as H2.
Balance rxn_005 with explicit reducing-equivalent bookkeeping.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This short hydrothermal route is attractive and literature-backed, but both steps are underspecified. rxn_008 should include H2 as coproduct, consistent with the reported hydrothermal oxidation of 2-hydroxyglutarate, and rxn_004 remains unbalanced because the reductive amination lacks explicit redox bookkeeping.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_008 as mol_012 -> mol_005 + H2 or an equivalently balanced oxidation step.
Rewrite rxn_004 with explicit reducing equivalents and balanced coproducts.
Clarify whether both reactions occur in the same hydrothermal regime.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the cleanest short hydrothermal concept. rxn_008 is missing the H2 coproduct reported in the literature, and rxn_005 is missing the reducing equivalent for FeS-mediated amination. If modeled explicitly, the H2 from rxn_008 could in principle feed rxn_005, but the current reaction nodes do not show that.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_008 with explicit H2 production.
Use that H2 or another explicit reductant in rxn_005 instead of leaving the reduction implicit.
Specify FeS surface conditions and hydrothermal parameters more explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Both component reactions are literature-motivated, but the combined route is weakly specified. rxn_009 lacks an explicit oxidant or reduced coproduct under cyanosulfidic conditions, rxn_004 is unbalanced, and the transfer of 2-oxoglutarate from a surface pool to a hydrothermal iron system is only implicit.
suggestions: Add the cyanosulfidic oxidant and reduced sulfur coproducts, or otherwise balance rxn_009 explicitly.
Rewrite rxn_004 with explicit reductant and coproducts.

The main issues remain the same: rxn_009 does not specify the oxidation partner under surface cyanosulfidic conditions, rxn_005 leaves the reducing equivalent implicit, and the cross-environment handoff of mol_005 is not modeled directly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The idea of generating 2-oxoglutarate and NH3 in one hydrothermal step is attractive, but rxn_011 is the weakest reaction in the network. It fails atom conservation and appears to be missing a C1 fragment and H2, suggesting a mis-specified decomposition chemistry or precursor identity. rxn_005 then adds a second unbalanced redox step.
suggestions: Re-check the identity and formula of mol_015 and the actual products of rxn_011; add the missing C1 byproduct if warranted by the source study.
Balance rxn_005 with an explicit reductant.
Verify the exact hydrothermal decomposition reported in the literature before keeping this branch.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest branch and the best aligned with the cited cyanosulfidic literature. rxn_006 is balanced as written, and rxn_007 is not a conservation violation because it is balanceable with small coefficients; it should simply be written explicitly as mol_010 + 4 mol_011 -> mol_008 + 2 mol_007. Surface conditions are appropriate and the pathway reaches glutamate cleanly.
suggestions: Write rxn_007 explicitly as mol_010 + 4 mol_011 -> mol_008 + 2 mol_007.
Annotate the surface conditions more specifically as aqueous cyanosulfidic chemistry.
If a fuller network is desired, connect mol_009 to upstream cyanosulfidic precursor formation.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected, literature-grounded network with an appropriate non-stereospecific glutamate target, but it is not approvable as submitted because the chemical specification is incomplete. The topology is coherent around 2-oxoglutarate plus an independent dinitrile branch, molecule IDs are consistent, and the environments generally match the cited hydrothermal and surface studies. However, the deterministic checker flags 6 of 11 reactions as UNBALANCED: rxn_003, rxn_004, rxn_005, rxn_008, rxn_009, and rxn_011. rxn_003 likely needs explicit H2 or another reductant; rxn_008 should release H2 hydrothermally; rxn_009 needs an explicit oxidant or reduced coproduct under cyanosulfidic conditions; rxn_004 and rxn_005 need explicit reducing-equivalent bookkeeping for reductive amination; and rxn_011 is the most serious defect because it is missing a C1 fragment and H2 and likely reflects a mis-specified precursor/product assignment. rxn_007 is acceptable in principle but should be written explicitly as mol_010 + 4 mol_011 -> mol_008 + 2 mol_007. Best current route is P10. Overall, the network aligns well with the literature conceptually, but the hydrothermal 2-oxoglutarate-centered branches need corrected stoichiometry and the mixed-environment routes would benefit from explicit handoff steps, so the network remains below the 0.90 approval threshold.
